glossary.definition: The claim an access token carries for group entitlements. Its shape decides what a policy can do: a delimited string ("[A, B]") forces text search; a JSON array (["A", "B"]) allows exact membership. The shape is decided at the token mapping, before any policy runs.

Searching for a group name inside a delimited-string claim. It is always inexact: MCPAccess-Atlan-Read-Extra matches a policy asking for MCPAccess-Atlan-Read, so a token can be granted a group it never held (the over-grant, reproduced in this lab).
Asking whether a JSON-array claim holds a value exactly. A decoy name never matches. This is what the token should enable, by carrying isMemberOf as a real array.

A group name that contains the policy's group as a substring but was never granted, such as MCPAccess-Atlan-Read-Extra. Give a test user the decoy only: the substring policy grants, the array policy refuses. The decoy pair is the proof that matching is exact.

This lab's in-process stand-in for the group-entitlement policy on an MCP gateway. It evaluates two claim-reading modes (exact array membership, substring search) over example group names, each compared exactly. It is not a policy engine and it decides nothing real.

sources.title: RFC 7519: JSON Web Token (JWT)
sources.use: A JWT claim value can be any JSON value, including an array; the string-vs-array question is about which one the token mapping emits.

cards.label: Mint both shapes
cards.description: Pick the shape and the groups, mint, and read the decoded claims: one token's isMemberOf is a delimited string, the other's a JSON array. Mock tokens, labelled.

cards.label: Case 2: the decoy over-grant
cards.description: A token that never held MCPAccess-Atlan-Read is granted it anyway when the policy searches text; the array policy refuses the same token. Simulated, reproducible.

stories.title: Two shapes, two answers
stories.text: A group-entitlement policy asks one question: does this token carry MCPAccess-Atlan-Read? When the token's isMemberOf is a delimited string the policy can only search text, and MCPAccess-Atlan-Read-Extra matches just as well. When it is a JSON array, membership is exact and the decoy is refused. The fix is a token-mapping change, and the decoy pair is the proof.
